principle: Show the observations, then the number they imply. A bare figure is false precision; the evidence behind it is intelligence a professional can judge.
what_is_proven: Every observation shown is measured, not modelled, and is final when it arrives.
The physics lands on the right absolute level: calibrating published dry-bean light-use efficiency and harvest index against USDA moved them by 5%.
The satellite independently identifies 2012 and 2013 as the worst years in 26 and 2023 as the best, without being told.
what_is_not_proven: That the estimate ranks one season against another correctly. Tested against USDA over 2016-2023 it did not, and the model's error cannot be separated from the scorecard's: USDA revised Nebraska's 2026 planted acres 21% inside one season, reports yield per HARVESTED acre so abandoned fields vanish from it, and stops publishing county yields in 2008.
That it holds outside the four states measured here.

what_would_sharpen_it.need: Real harvest data — loads, test weights, screen size, tied to place and date
what_would_sharpen_it.why: The single largest gap. Six methods failed against public yield data because it is aggregated, revised and late, not because the methods are wrong. A few hundred real observations make every one of them testable again.
what_would_sharpen_it.how: A grower and agronomist web app reporting against the model, season by season

what_would_sharpen_it.why: An irrigated and a dryland field under identical weather are different crops. USDA stopped publishing the split in 2008.
what_would_sharpen_it.how: USGS MIrAD-US irrigated-land mapping, plus what growers report directly

what_would_sharpen_it.why: 250 m mixes bean ground with what surrounds it. Sentinel-2 at 10 m resolves individual fields.
The mask is 2024; USDA publishes 2026's in January 2027. Beans rotate.
what_would_sharpen_it.how: In-season classification from the same satellite series

scope_today: Four states, seven growing regions. The method is not specific to them — the same public sources cover the United States and Canada, and the crop physics is not regional.

evidence.source: satellite, on ground USDA maps as dry beans

evidence.what: Water the crop actually got, through flowering and pod fill
evidence.source: OpenET — measures water used, so it sees irrigation

estimate.basis: sunlight and canopy from satellite, temperature from local stations, water use from OpenET, converted with published dry-bean light-use efficiency and harvest index
